profile.name: Prayash Bartaula
profile.title: Full-Stack Developer
profile.tagline: I build the interface, and the engine behind it.
profile.short_bio: Full-stack developer in Hetauda, Nepal. I take web products from an empty repository to a working URL — schema, API, interface, and the motion in between.
profile.bio:
I'm a full-stack developer based in Hetauda, Nepal. I work across the whole stack because I want to own the whole outcome: the data model, the API, the interface, and the way it all feels under a cursor.

Most of what I know came from building something, deciding it wasn't good enough, and building it again. I'm studying BSc. CSIT at Hetauda City College, but the work on this page came from shipping projects rather than from coursework.

I care about detail more than is strictly efficient. I would rather spend another day on how a page loads than move on with something that only mostly works. What I'm building toward is international client work, and eventually a product company of my own.
profile.availability_note: Open to freelance projects and full-time roles, remote or relocating.

projects.name: Software Company Website
projects.summary: A marketing site for a software business, structured around one sequence: what the company does, why it can be trusted, and how to start a conversation.
projects.description:
A company site has a narrow job, and most of them fail by burying it under decoration. I built this one as a straight line — capability, credibility, contact — and let typography and spacing carry the weight instead of effects. Motion marks the transition between sections and nothing else.

The layouts change shape between breakpoints rather than scaling down, so the narrow view is its own composition instead of a squeezed copy of the wide one.

projects.name: Mero Bhariya
projects.summary: A multi-page platform running on its own domain, built to carry a complete user journey rather than a single page.
projects.description:
This build passed the size where you can hold the whole thing in your head, which is exactly where structure starts to earn its keep: components that stay consistent, state that stays predictable, and routes that stay readable as they multiply.

It runs on its own domain, so DNS, deployment and asset delivery were part of the work rather than something that happened afterwards. Shipping it taught me more about the last ten percent of a project than anything else here.

projects.name: Game of Thrones
projects.summary: A themed interactive site — an exercise in committing hard to an atmosphere and letting every other decision follow from it.
projects.description:
Built as a study in atmosphere. Dark palette, heavy display type, transitions timed to feel deliberate rather than fast. The question I was answering was how far a visual direction can be pushed before it stops being usable — then pulling back to the line just before that.

Useful because restraint is easier to learn from the other side of it.

projects.name: Cafe
projects.summary: A cafe site built around the two things a visitor actually came for, with the atmosphere arranged around them.
projects.description:
Hospitality sites fail in a predictable way: they lead with mood and bury the practical information. I put the menu and the essentials where someone hungry looks first, then used imagery and generous spacing to carry the atmosphere around them.

This one was built narrow-first. Most people looking up a cafe are already outside, on a phone, in a hurry.

projects.name: Restaurant
projects.summary: A second run at the hospitality brief, which made it the most useful comparison in this set.
projects.description:
Coming back to a problem I had already solved once turned out to be more instructive than starting something new. I could see which decisions had carried over, which had only looked clever the first time, and where the earlier build had been more complicated than the job required.

The menu structure and the path to getting in touch took most of the attention.

services.name: Full-Stack Web Development

services.name: Frontend Engineering
services.description: Interfaces built for speed and for feel. Component architecture that survives a second round of features, layouts that hold from a narrow phone to a wide desktop, and motion that directs attention instead of competing for it.

services.name: Backend & API Development
services.description: REST APIs with real authentication, validation on every input, and error handling that stays useful in production. The schema gets designed before the first endpoint is written, because that is the part you cannot fix cheaply later.

services.name: 3D & Interactive Experiences
services.description: WebGL scenes that hold their frame rate on ordinary devices, with a graceful fallback when they cannot. Used where depth and interaction actually earn their weight — not sprinkled over a page as decoration.
